newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran say to allow foreign banks into free zones.
newsitem.headline: Iran say to allow foreign banks into free zones.

text.p: Iran has plans to allow foreign banks to establish branches in its free trade zones, Iranian Central Bank Governor Mohsen Nourbakhsh said on Monday.
Nourbakhsh, quoted by the official Iranian news agency IRNA, said the government decided on the plan, which also included authorising partly private-owned Iranian banks in the zones.

He said the plan was based on a decree by Iran's Expediency Discernment Council, which arbitrates between the parliament and the Guardian Council, a body of lawyers and Shi'ite Moslem clerics that vets parliamentary laws for conformity with Islam and the constitution. Nourbakhsh did not give further details.
The plan appeared to be the result of legislation passed by the parliament last year to ease foreign exchange rules in free trade zones set up to attract foreign investment.
Parliament amended the law after objections by the Guardian Council. Iran set up free trade zones on 1989 in Kish and Qeshm islands in the Gulf and in the southeastern port of Chahbahar.
